diary.title: 1. Relevant evidence
diary.question: In this fictional adult sample, did a sleep diary help participants describe their sleep routine?

sources.title: Diary workshop: adult pilot
sources.design: Pilot; self-reported descriptions; no clinical outcome
sources.relevance: Directly addresses the adult diary question
sources.passage: In this fictional pilot, adults using a diary gave more detailed descriptions of their sleep routines after one week. The pilot did not measure sleep improvement.
sources.finding: The fictional pilot reports more detailed descriptions of sleep routines.
sources.limit: Self-reported pilot data; no evidence of improved sleep.
sources.document: A one-week fictional workshop compared descriptions before and after diary use. The sample was small and there was no control group. The outcome was how much detail people included, not a clinical sleep measure. All data and organisations in this document are invented for interaction testing.

sources.title: Student timetable preferences
sources.relevance: Timetabling, not diary use or sleep descriptions
sources.passage: Fictional students preferred later study-group meetings. No diary or sleep-description outcome was measured.
sources.document: This invented poll concerns study-group scheduling. It provides no evidence about diaries. It is a deliberately irrelevant retrieval result.

sources.title: Earlier diary survey, withdrawn version
sources.passage: This fictional earlier record has been withdrawn. Its methods and results cannot be inspected.
sources.document: This invented archive entry represents a withdrawn or unusable result. Age alone does not determine validity; this record is unsuitable because the underlying methods are unavailable and the record is withdrawn.

additional_sources.title: Adult sleep diary: workshop follow-up
additional_sources.population: Adults returning to the fictional diary workshop
additional_sources.relevance: Adult diary use and detail in sleep-routine descriptions
additional_sources.passage: In this fictional follow-up, returning adults used diary entries to describe the timing of their sleep routines in more detail. Sleep quality and clinical benefit were not measured.
additional_sources.finding: The fictional follow-up reports more detailed descriptions of sleep-routine timing.
additional_sources.limit: Returning volunteers only; no control group or measured sleep improvement.
additional_sources.document: This invented follow-up asked returning workshop volunteers to describe their routines with their diary available. It measured the detail of those descriptions, not the accuracy of diary entries or any health outcome. All organisations and findings are fictional.

additional_sources.title: Diary notebook cover preferences
additional_sources.relevance: Mentions diaries but measures notebook appearance, not sleep descriptions
additional_sources.passage: Fictional notebook shoppers preferred a larger diary cover illustration. The survey did not test sleep diaries or the detail of routine descriptions.
additional_sources.limit: Different purpose and outcome; no evidence for the diary question.
additional_sources.document: This invented design survey concerns notebook covers and page colour. Its use of the word diary is a keyword match only. No sleep-related activity was observed and no routine descriptions were collected.

additional_sources.title: Sleep diary comparison: withdrawn dataset
additional_sources.relevance: Related diary question, but the comparison cannot be inspected
additional_sources.passage: This fictional sleep-diary comparison was withdrawn after its underlying dataset became unavailable. No inspectable comparison remains.
additional_sources.limit: Withdrawn and uncheckable; its publication date alone is not the reason for exclusion.
additional_sources.document: This invented archive record represents missing underlying evidence. The former diary comparison cannot support a finding because its methods and data cannot be checked. It is not rejected simply because it is older.

conflict.title: 2. Conflicting evidence
conflict.question: Do these fictional adult studies agree about the effect of the Example Wind-Down exercise on self-rated calmness?

sources.title: Wind-Down pilot A
sources.passage: In fictional pilot A, participants reported greater calmness after the Example Wind-Down exercise. The small uncontrolled sample limits interpretation.
sources.finding: Pilot A reports greater self-rated calmness.
sources.document: This invented pilot measures a subjective rating. No claim of clinical effectiveness is supported. The contrast with pilot B is scripted to exercise a disagreement state.

sources.title: Wind-Down pilot B
sources.passage: In fictional pilot B, participants reported no change in calmness after the Example Wind-Down exercise. The small sample limits interpretation.
sources.finding: Pilot B reports no change in self-rated calmness.
sources.limit: Small sample; a different pilot cohort.
sources.document: This invented pilot uses the same named exercise and outcome but a different sample. Conflicting findings do not establish why results differ. The simulator does not estimate an overall effect.

sources.title: Exercise promotion leaflet
sources.relevance: Mentions exercise but supplies no outcome evidence
sources.passage: This fictional promotional leaflet describes the exercise but reports no observations or comparison.
sources.document: This invented leaflet is a relevance trap. A matching keyword does not make a document suitable evidence.

additional_sources.title: Wind-Down pilot C: adult calmness ratings
additional_sources.population: Fictional adult volunteers in a third cohort
additional_sources.relevance: Same Example Wind-Down exercise and calmness outcome
additional_sources.passage: In fictional pilot C, adult volunteers reported greater calmness after the Example Wind-Down exercise. The small uncontrolled cohort does not resolve the disagreement between earlier pilots.
additional_sources.finding: Pilot C reports greater self-rated calmness in another fictional adult cohort.
additional_sources.limit: Small uncontrolled cohort; no estimate of overall effect or clinical benefit.
additional_sources.document: This invented third pilot uses the same named exercise and a subjective calmness rating. Its positive finding can be compared with pilots A and B, but counting pilots is not a valid synthesis. The simulator makes no overall-effect estimate.

additional_sources.title: Wind-Down audio clarity survey
additional_sources.design: Audio usability survey; no calmness measurement
additional_sources.relevance: Same exercise name but a different outcome
additional_sources.passage: Fictional volunteers could hear the Wind-Down audio instructions clearly. No calmness rating or change in calmness was measured.
additional_sources.limit: Audio clarity does not establish the effect of the exercise on calmness.
additional_sources.document: This invented usability exercise checks sound levels and clarity of instructions. It does not evaluate the effect of the Example Wind-Down exercise. Shared terminology does not make it evidence for the research question.

additional_sources.title: Archived Wind-Down claim: withdrawn analysis
additional_sources.design: Withdrawn analysis; data and methods unavailable
additional_sources.relevance: Mentions the exercise but supplies no inspectable evidence
additional_sources.passage: This fictional archived Wind-Down analysis was withdrawn. The source no longer provides its data, methods or usable calmness results.
additional_sources.limit: Withdrawn and unavailable evidence; age alone is not a quality judgement.
additional_sources.document: This invented record models an uncheckable claim. It cannot resolve the disagreement among the fictional pilots because its analysis has been withdrawn and the original observations are unavailable.

insufficient.title: 3. Insufficient evidence
insufficient.question: Do these fictional sources establish whether a wearable sleep score is useful for schoolchildren?

sources.title: Wearable usability in adults
sources.passage: Fictional adults could find the score display. No schoolchildren were included, and the score was not validated as a health measure.
sources.document: This invented task measures whether adults can locate a screen element. It does not test usefulness for schoolchildren. Selecting this document cannot establish the requested conclusion.

sources.title: Device packaging guide
sources.passage: The fictional packaging guide lists box dimensions and label positions. It contains no evaluation of sleep scores.
sources.document: This invented source demonstrates an irrelevant result returned by a noisy retrieval stage.

sources.title: Archived wearable claim
sources.passage: This fictional archived claim was withdrawn; no inspectable data remain.
sources.document: This invented record represents unavailable underlying evidence. Do not interpret its date as an automatic quality score.

additional_sources.title: Adult wearable sleep-score interface study
additional_sources.design: Interface-navigation task; no validation of sleep scores
additional_sources.relevance: Adult navigation findings do not address usefulness for schoolchildren
additional_sources.passage: Fictional adult office volunteers located the wearable sleep-score explanation screen. The task did not include schoolchildren or test whether the score was useful or valid.
additional_sources.limit: Wrong population and outcome; no evidence for children's health or score usefulness.
additional_sources.document: This invented interface study measures whether adults find an information screen. It supplies no observations about schoolchildren and does not evaluate any health conclusion. A further search in this small fictional collection cannot create missing child-specific evidence.

additional_sources.title: Schoolchildren's wearable strap preferences
additional_sources.population: Fictional schoolchildren in a design workshop
additional_sources.design: Strap colour and fit preferences; no sleep-score evaluation
additional_sources.relevance: Matching population but a different task and outcome
additional_sources.passage: In a fictional workshop, schoolchildren chose preferred wearable strap colours and sizes. No sleep scores, health measures or usefulness outcomes were collected.
additional_sources.limit: Matching the population does not compensate for the missing sleep-score outcome.
additional_sources.document: This invented classroom design activity concerns appearance and strap fit. It provides no evidence about the usefulness or validity of wearable sleep scores for schoolchildren. It is included to demonstrate an outcome mismatch despite an apparently relevant population.

additional_sources.title: Children's sleep-score claim: withdrawn record
additional_sources.design: Withdrawn illustrative claim; underlying data missing
additional_sources.relevance: Matching topic, but no inspectable data can support a conclusion
additional_sources.passage: This fictional claim about children's wearable sleep scores was withdrawn. Its underlying data and methods are unavailable for inspection.
additional_sources.limit: Withdrawn and uncheckable; no usable evidence for the schoolchildren question.
additional_sources.document: This invented archive record deliberately resembles a relevant search hit, but no data remain. Its date is not an automatic quality score. The record cannot support a health conclusion or the usefulness of a sleep score.
